chapter: Sidemen, the Hampton years, race and money
title: Dannie Richmond
summary: Mingus says Richmond now leans toward rock but knows his music best; Johnson recalls Richmond guiding him at the Showplace.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: How about Danny? Danny's been with you for a long time, and I never have heard anybody who -- I mean, he really is the other half of your heartbeat sometimes. I mean, he just knows what you're going to do.

He used to be, but in the last five years, I wouldn't say that. He's auditioning for a rock band all the time. Hoping some rock players will hear him. He stopped playing my music a long time ago. He was still playing the basic part of it, but his choice of cymbals and his beat is rock. (Inaudible) or that little kid that played with Miles Davis.
sock cymbal, which I don't dig.
Well, Danny was a tenor player when you first --
He still knows my music better than anybody else. All the compositions.

During that tiny period that I -- at the Showplace, when I played in the band, he -- the only reason I knew what was going on was that he would turn around and tell me what was going on, this is what's going to happen now. He was singing licks to me and telling me everything that was happening. And -- because very little was written out. A few chord symbols and things like that.
